0x61b1af0.name: rocksdb::Tracer::Write
quirks: On the skip path Write returns Status::OK() without consulting the clock: a flagged or oversized write leaves the clock's call count at 0 and the sampling counter untouched (flag skips) -- the gate runs before the timestamp is read.

The varint length prefix encodes the LOW 32 bits of the batch size (mov esi, r13d before EncodeVarint32) while the append copies the full size_t -- a >4 GiB batch would prefix the truncated length; untestable at that scale, recorded from the disassembly.
The payload_map bit (kWriteBatchData = 1, map becomes 2) is never serialized by EncodeTrace; it is visible only as the first 8 payload bytes (PutFixed64).

The timestamp comes from the 13-layer SystemClockWrapper::NowMicros fast path (each layer's vtable slot 19 compared against 0x5d4d490, followed through +0x20); the first layer whose slot differs calls that slot's function directly instead of continuing the chain.

The batch's data pointer is [batch+0x40] and its size [batch+0x48] -- rep_ is the std::string at batch+0x40, confirmed by WriteBatch::Clear (0x5fb7220), which resizes that string to the 12-byte rep header.

The two landing pads (the .cold part at 0x61b1ac6..0x61b1aeb and the separate 37-byte FDE at 0x61b1e18..0x61b1e3d, _M_dispose + _Unwind_Resume) run only on the exception path (bad_alloc from the string appends) and are not modelled; the string length guards raise length_error instead (std::string::_M_append, via __throw_length_error).

The payload string is freed only when its pointer differs from the SSO buffer at rsp+0x48 (standard string destruction); the 5-byte varint buffer sits at rsp+0x63, just below the stack canary at rsp+0x68.
rules: if ShouldSkipTrace(this, type) (0x61b1930) returns true, return Status::OK() at once (no clock call, no writer call)
trace.ts = clock_->NowMicros() via the 13-layer SystemClockWrapper::NowMicros (0x5d4d490) fast path (vtable slot 19, +0x20 per layer); a layer whose slot differs calls that slot's function directly
TracerHelper::SetPayloadMap(trace.payload_map, 1) (0x61b18b0): bts bit 1 (kWriteBatchData), so the in-memory payload_map becomes 2
PutFixed64(&trace.payload, trace.payload_map): append the 8 little-endian bytes of the map (02 00 00 00 00 00 00 00), with the std::string length guard

PutLengthPrefixedSlice(&trace.payload, batch->Data()): EncodeVarint32((uint32_t)batch_size) into a 5-byte stack buffer, append the varint bytes, then append the batch's rep bytes ([batch+0x40], [batch+0x48] bytes), each append with the std::string length guard
return WriteTrace(trace) (0x61b1a10): EncodeTrace + TraceWriter::Write (slot 2); the returned Status is forwarded unchanged
